reading.title: Bioluminescence in Deep Sea Organisms
reading.passage: Bioluminescence is the production of light by living organisms through chemical reactions. Many deep-sea creatures use this ability to communicate, attract prey, and navigate in complete darkness. For example, the anglerfish uses a glowing lure to attract smaller fish, while certain jellyfish produce light to confuse predators. Scientists estimate that over 90% of deep-sea creatures possess some form of bioluminescence, making it one of nature's most remarkable adaptations to extreme environments.

questions.q: According to the passage, what is the primary function of bioluminescence in anglerfish?
questions.explanation: 글에서 'the anglerfish uses a glowing lure to attract smaller fish'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 B입니다.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a function of bioluminescence?
questions.explanation: 문장에서 bioluminescence의 기능으로 communicate, attract prey, navigate이 언급되지만, 열을 생산하는 것은 언급되지 않습니다. 정답은 D입니다.

questions.q: What percentage of deep-sea creatures are estimated to have bioluminescence?
questions.explanation: 글의 마지막 문장에서 'over 90% of deep-sea creatures possess some form of bioluminescence'라고 명시되어 있습니다. 정답은 C입니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement: Technology has made human relationships weaker rather than stronger? Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer.

structure.intro: 명확한 입장 표현 (동의 또는 불동의) + 주요 이유 2-3개 미리 언급. 예: 'I disagree with this statement because technology has actually strengthened human relationships through increased connectivity and accessibility.'
structure.body1: 첫 번째 이유 전개: 소셜 미디어와 SNS가 먼 거리의 사람들을 연결하는 방식. 구체적 예시 제시 (예: 장거리 연애, 해외 가족과의 연락).
structure.body2: 두 번째 이유 전개: 온라인 커뮤니티의 형성과 공통 관심사를 가진 사람들의 만남. 추가 예시 (예: 온라인 학습 그룹, 취미 커뮤니티).
structure.conclusion: 주요 논점 재정리 + 반박 가능한 입장 인정 + 최종 의견 제시. 예: 'While face-to-face interaction remains important, technology has provided unprecedented opportunities to strengthen relationships.'

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to study alone in a quiet environment. Others prefer to study in groups with classmates. Which do you prefer and why?
useful_expressions: In my opinion, I prefer studying alone because...
One reason is that I can concentrate better without distractions.
Another advantage is that I can study at my own pace.
Furthermore, studying in groups helps with discussing difficult concepts.
However, some people might argue that...
To summarize, I believe that studying alone is more effective for me because...
sample_points: 집중력 향상: 혼자 공부할 때 방해 요소가 없어 더 집중할 수 있으며, 자신의 페이스에 맞춰 학습 가능
효율성: 원하는 시간에 원하는 과목을 공부할 수 있고, 모르는 부분을 깊이 있게 이해할 수 있음
대안적 관점: 그룹 스터디는 다양한 관점 공유와 어려운 개념 토론의 장점이 있지만, 시간 낭비 가능성 존재

listening.title: University Library Resources
listening.script: Student: Excuse me, I'm looking for information about research databases for my paper on climate change. Librarian: Of course! We have several excellent resources. Our main database is JSTOR, which contains thousands of peer-reviewed articles on environmental science. We also have access to Google Scholar, which is free and comprehensive. Additionally, we offer one-on-one research consultations if you need help navigating these resources. Student: That sounds helpful. How long do these consultations usually take? Librarian: Typically, they last about 30 minutes to an hour, depending on your needs. You can book an appointment online through our website, or you can visit our reference desk during business hours. We also have a chat service available in the evenings for quick questions. Many students find this very convenient. Student: I'll definitely check that out. Thank you so much for your help!

questions.q: What is the main topic of this conversation?
options: Available library resources and research assistance
questions.explanation: 대화의 중심은 학생이 도서관의 리서치 데이터베이스와 도움말 서비스에 대해 물어보는 것입니다. 따라서 정답은 B입니다.

questions.q: According to the librarian, how long do research consultations typically last?
questions.explanation: 사서가 'Typically, they last about 30 minutes to an hour, depending on your needs'라고 명확히 말했습니다. 정답은 B입니다.

questions.q: What are the ways students can access research consultations according to the conversation?
options: Online booking, reference desk, or chat service
questions.explanation: 사서는 '온라인 예약, 레퍼런스 데스크 방문, 저녁의 채팅 서비스' 세 가지 방법을 제시했습니다. 정답은 B입니다.
